newsitem.title: USA: Apple second-quarter loss less than expected.
newsitem.headline: Apple second-quarter loss less than expected.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. reported a loss for the latest quarter that was far lower than Wall Street expected, but said it will not return to profitability later this year, as it had predicted.

The computer maker said unit shipments of its Macintosh personal computer fell 17 percent in the quarter, but strong sales abroad and to schools in the United States produced better-than-expected revenue. Apple also cut costs more aggressively than analysts had expected.

"They made a very strong comeback in Japan because of Powerbook (laptops), and they did very well in U.S. educational markets," said William Milton at investment bank Brown Brothers Harriman in New York.

For its fiscal third quarter ended June 27, Apple lost $56 million, or 44 cents a share, compared with a loss of $32 million, or 26 cents a share, a year earlier. Last year's results included a $39 million gain from the sale of an investment.
Wall Steet expected Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., to post a loss of 61 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.
Revenue fell 23 percent to $1.7 billion from $2.2 billion.
Some analysts had expected Apple to report a disastrous quarter because the company's board of directors ousted Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gilbert Amelio last week.

The company said at the time that it was "getting out of the business of predicting" results. Earlier this year, company executives had said Apple could report a profit as early as the September quarter.
"Everyone had feared the worst," said Daniel Kunstler at J.P. Morgan. "I was braced for an implosion of unit shipments."
Still, Apple said it will not report a profit later this year.

"Right now what we're doing is reviewing all of our product road maps," said Fred Anderson, Apple's chief financial officer and interim CEO. "Anything that doesn't create value for our customers in our core markets has got to be on our list" of cuts.
Anderson also said the company was close to hiring an executive search firm to find a new CEO, a process that could take up to three months.

He also said Apple will not need to raise more cash any time soon, despite the prospect of continuing losses. Apple ended the quarter with a little more than $1 billion in cash, down from $1.3 billion in the March quarter.

For the nine months, Apple reported a loss of $884 million, or $7.04 a share, compared with a loss of $841 million, or $6.81 a share, a year earlier. Apple has now lost money in six of the last seven quarters.
Sales fell to $5.5 billion from $7.5 billion in the nine months.
